programs.name: Beta-to-alpha transdifferentiation
programs.function: Ectopic activation of alpha-cell lineage genes with loss of beta-cell identity

programs.name: Lipid uptake and handling
programs.function: Fatty acid uptake, intracellular lipid trafficking, and lipid droplet buffering

programs.name: Fatty acid oxidation
programs.function: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation and lipid-derived energy metabolism

programs.name: Lipotoxic stress
programs.function: Cellular stress from excess saturated fatty acids and toxic lipid intermediates

states.name: Mature functional beta cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy beta cell
states.notes: Canonical mature beta-cell identity/function panel (transcription factors, hormone, prohormone convertase, glucose sensing, KATP channel); textbook/consensus markers used across human islet single-cell atlases (e.g., Segerstolpe et al. 2016 Cell Metab).

states.name: Secretory-adapted beta cell
states.phenotype: Prolonged insulin demand; compensation, obesity, or pregnancy
states.notes: Reflects physiological (adaptive, non-terminal) UPR activation and increased prohormone-processing/secretory-granule capacity that accompanies compensatory insulin demand in pregnancy/obesity, distinct from the maladaptive terminal UPR of the er-stressed state (Lipson et al. 2006; Scheuner & Kaufman 2008 Endocr Rev).

states.name: ER-stressed beta cell
states.phenotype: Beta cell undergoing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress

states.name: Inflammatory response beta cell
states.phenotype: Typical of early T1D or cytokine-driven inflammatory exposure
states.notes: Type I/II interferon-stimulated gene and MHC-I hyperexpression signature described in early/insulitic T1D beta cells (Russell et al. 2019 Diabetes; Marroqui et al. 2017 studies of cytokine-exposed islets).

states.name: Glucolipotoxicity beta cell
states.phenotype: Combined high glucose and elevated lipid exposure, often associated with metabolic stress in T2D
states.notes: Combined high glucose (TXNIP induction) and elevated free fatty acid signature (lipid droplet/ceramide/lipogenic and oxidative-stress genes) seen in glucolipotoxic beta-cell models relevant to T2D (Poitout & Robertson 2008 Endocr Rev; Cnop lab lipotoxicity/ceramide studies).

states.name: Dedifferentiated beta cell
states.phenotype: Loss of mature beta-cell identity toward an ALDH1A3+ progenitor-like state, described in type 2 diabetes and aging
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. Loss of mature identity toward a progenitor/multipotent-like and 'disallowed-gene'-expressing state: ALDH1A3/SOX9/NEUROG3/HES1/GATA6/FOXO1(nuclear exclusion) from Talchai et al. 2012 Cell and Cinti et al. 2016 JCEM (human T2D); LDHA/SLC16A1 are classic 'disallowed genes' re-expressed on identity loss (Pullen & Rutter 2013); SMOC1 is a newly identified (2025) alpha-lineage gene ectopically induced in dedifferentiating beta cells.

states.name: Transdifferentiated beta cell
states.phenotype: Beta-to-alpha lineage conversion with ectopic glucagon expression, an extreme form of beta-cell plasticity reported in longstanding diabetes
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. Beta-to-alpha lineage conversion signature (ectopic acquisition of full alpha-cell transcriptional program) from human islet studies of longstanding diabetes (Spijker et al. 2015 Diabetes; SMOC1 trajectory-inference paper, Nat Commun 2025).

states.name: Proliferating beta cell
states.phenotype: Compensatory beta-cell replication seen in pregnancy, obesity, and early compensatory hyperplasia; identity is largely retained while cycling
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. Compensatory replication signature retaining identity genes; FOXM1/CCND2/PLK1/CENPA axis and BIRC5 are established drivers of adaptive human beta-cell proliferation in obesity/pregnancy (Zhong lab FoxM1 studies; Aguayo-Mazzucato/Bonner-Weir compensatory expansion literature).

states.name: Senescent beta cell
states.phenotype: Cell-cycle-arrested, apoptosis-resistant beta cell with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), implicated in aging and type 2 diabetes
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. p16/CDKN2A (stable arrest) and p21/CDKN1A (early arrest) plus SASP factors (GDF15, SERPINE1/PAI-1, CCL2, IL1B) from Aguayo-Mazzucato et al. 2019 Cell Metab and Thompson et al. 2019 Cell Metab; B2M was used as a cell-surface sorting marker for senescent human beta cells in the same studies; GLB1 encodes SA-beta-galactosidase, the classical senescence enzyme marker.

programs.name: Dedifferentiation / transdifferentiation
programs.function: Loss of alpha identity and drift toward a beta-like or progenitor state

states.name: Mature functional alpha cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy alpha cell
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. Canonical alpha-cell identity/marker panel including transcription factors and human-alpha-enriched surface/secreted markers identified in single-cell islet atlases (LOXL4, CRYBA2, GC, SLC7A2 recur across human alpha-cell scRNA-seq studies; SLC7A2 confirmed functionally required for alpha-cell proliferation/secretion, JCI 2024).

states.name: Hyperglucagonemic alpha cell
states.phenotype: Chronic hyperglycemia-driven overactivity seen in T2D
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes because a distinct human single-cell transcriptomic signature for chronic hyperglucagonemia (as opposed to physiology) is not well established. SLC38A5/SLC7A2 amino-acid transporter induction is documented in the liver-alpha-cell axis literature on glucagon receptor resistance/hyperglucagonemia (Kim et al. 2017 Cell Metab; Dean lab SLC7A2 studies, JCI 2024); remaining genes reflect increased glucagon biosynthetic machinery.

states.name: Dedifferentiated alpha cell
states.phenotype: Loss of alpha identity reported in long-standing T1D and T2D
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes as human evidence for alpha-cell dedifferentiation is much thinner than for beta cells. PAX4 gain and reduced ARX with increased NKX6.1 in alpha cells accompanying reduced beta-cell mass was directly shown in human pancreas (Sci Rep 2021, 'Increased NKX6.1... decreased ARX expression in alpha cells'); SOX9/GATA6/HES1 are shared progenitor-reversion markers by analogy to beta-cell dedifferentiation literature.

states.name: Inflammatory response alpha cell
states.phenotype: Cytokine and interferon exposure typical of insulitis in T1D
states.notes: Interferon-stimulated gene/MHC-I signature also documented in alpha cells during insulitis, with alpha cells showing even stronger basal and induced immune/HLA responses than beta cells in T1D single-cell studies (Russell et al. 2019 Diabetes).

states.name: Mature functional delta cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy delta cell providing paracrine inhibition of insulin and glucagon release
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch. HHEX, RBP4, LEPR (leptin receptor), and GHSR (ghrelin receptor, mediates paracrine ghrelin regulation of somatostatin secretion) are established delta-cell-enriched markers from purified islet-subpopulation transcriptomics (Adriaenssens et al. 2016 Diabetologia; DiGruccio et al. 2016 Mol Metab).

states.name: Hypersecretory delta cell
states.phenotype: Increased somatostatin tone reported in some models of islet dysfunction and aging
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes because a discrete 'hypersecretory' delta-cell transcriptional state is not clearly defined in the literature. Genes reflect somatostatin biosynthesis/secretion machinery and the known leptin-LEPR and ghrelin-GHSR regulatory loops shown to modulate delta-cell somatostatin output (leptin regulates delta-cell somatostatin secretion, ADA meeting abstract/Diabetes 2023; Adriaenssens et al. 2016).

states.name: Inflammatory response delta cell
states.phenotype: Cytokine/interferon exposure typical of insulitis
states.notes: Same class-wide interferon/MHC-I response documented across islet endocrine cell types (including delta cells) during insulitis (Russell et al. 2019 Diabetes).

states.name: Reduced/dysfunctional delta cell
states.phenotype: Loss of delta-cell mass and function reported in longstanding diabetes
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes because the literature (Somatostatin-containing delta-cell number is reduced in Type 2 Diabetes, PMC9959292) documents reduced delta-cell mass/number in T2D rather than a well-defined distinct transcriptional signature of surviving/declining cells. Genes reflect diminished identity-gene dosage plus the intrinsic apoptosis pathway implicated in cell loss.

programs.name: Pancreatic polypeptide biosynthesis
programs.function: Production and processing of pancreatic polypeptide

states.name: Mature functional gamma cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy PP cell regulating pancreatic exocrine secretion and appetite via PPY
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes reflecting the limited literature specifically characterizing this rare/understudied cell type. Markers drawn from human islet single-cell atlases that resolve a distinct PPY+ gamma/PP-cell cluster (Segerstolpe et al. 2016 Cell Metab; Muraro et al. 2016 Cell Systems).

states.name: Stressed gamma cell
states.phenotype: Secretory-overload ER stress state
states.notes: No PP/gamma-cell-specific stress transcriptomic study was found; genes are inferred from the generic UPR pathway shared across secretory endocrine cells rather than from direct published PP-cell data. Flagged as lower-confidence/generic.

states.name: Inflammatory response gamma cell
states.phenotype: Cytokine/interferon exposure typical of insulitis
states.notes: PP-cell-specific single-cell data are sparse, but islet-wide interferon-stimulated gene induction during insulitis is documented to affect all endocrine cell types, including PP cells (Russell et al. 2019 Diabetes).

states.name: Mature functional epsilon cell
states.phenotype: Ghrelin-producing cell, abundant in fetal islets and rare in the healthy adult pancreas
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes because epsilon cells are rare (~1% of adult islet cells) and poorly studied. GHRL/ISL1/NKX2-2 co-expression (notably without NKX6-1 or PAX6) is directly documented in human fetal and adult pancreas (Andralojc et al. 2009 Diabetologia); MBOAT4 (ghrelin O-acyltransferase) is required for ghrelin activation.

states.name: Developmental (neonatal-like) epsilon cell
states.phenotype: Expanded epsilon-cell population characteristic of the fetal and neonatal pancreas
states.notes: Verified via WebSearch; fewer than 10 genes, thin literature. Reflects the expanded ghrelin+ population (~10% of islet cells at midgestation vs ~1% in adults) and sporadic co-production with pancreatic polypeptide reported in fetal/neonatal human pancreas (Andralojc et al. 2009 Diabetologia; Upchurch/Wierup developmental epsilon-cell literature).

states.name: Stressed epsilon cell
states.phenotype: ER-stress/apoptotic state
states.notes: No published data describe a specific stress/ER-stress or apoptotic transcriptional state for epsilon cells; this cell type is essentially unstudied in this context. Genes listed are purely inferred from the generic UPR/apoptosis pathways shared by secretory endocrine cells and should be treated as placeholders, not literature-confirmed markers, until primary epsilon-cell stress data exist.

programs.name: Digestive enzyme biosynthesis
programs.function: Production of proteases, lipases, and amylase for digestion

programs.name: Zymogen granule biology
programs.function: Packaging and regulated exocytosis of digestive zymogens

programs.name: Zymogen activation control
programs.function: Protection against premature intracellular trypsinogen activation

programs.name: Unfolded protein response
programs.function: Adaptive ER stress from very high secretory burden

programs.name: Acinar-to-ductal metaplasia
programs.function: Dedifferentiation toward a ductal-like progenitor state, a precursor process in pancreatitis and PanIN/PDAC initiation

states.name: Mature functional acinar cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy acinar cell producing digestive enzymes
states.notes: Canonical acinar identity transcription factors (PTF1A/RBPJL/NR5A2/BHLHA15 form the core acinar specification complex) plus the digestive-enzyme and zymogen-granule programs constitutively expressed by healthy acinar cells. Well established textbook biology (Masui/MacDonald acinar TF network; Logsdon & Ji enzyme biosynthesis reviews).

states.name: Pancreatitis-associated acinar cell
states.phenotype: Premature zymogen activation and ER stress characteristic of acute/chronic pancreatitis
states.notes: PRSS1/SPINK1/CTRC are the classic hereditary/chronic pancreatitis susceptibility genes governing premature trypsinogen activation and its control. CTSB drives lysosomal cathepsin B-mediated intra-acinar trypsinogen activation, the initiating event of acute pancreatitis (Halangk et al., J Clin Invest, 2000). HSPA5/DDIT3/XBP1/ATF4 reflect the unfolded protein response documented in pancreatitis acinar cells (Ji & Logsdon lab studies on ER stress in pancreatitis). NFKBIA/IL6/TNF/CXCL1 reflect NF-kB-driven acinar cell-intrinsic inflammatory signaling shown to be an early, causal event in experimental pancreatitis (Gukovsky & Gukovskaya reviews on NF-kB in pancreatitis). REG3A (rat homolog PAP, 'pancreatitis-associated protein') is a long-established acute-phase/regenerative gene induced specifically in pancreatitis.

states.name: Metaplastic (ADM) acinar cell
states.phenotype: KRAS-driven acinar-to-ductal metaplasia, a precursor state to PanIN in pancreatic cancer
states.notes: KRT19/SOX9/ONECUT1/HNF1B mark the duct-like transcriptional switch in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM); KRAS oncogene drives the transition (Kopp et al., Cancer Cell, 2012, Sox9-dependent ADM initiation of PDAC). TFF2/TFF1/MUC6/MUC1/SPDEF mark the 'mucinous/pyloric metaplasia' intermediate identified by single-cell profiling of ADM (Ma et al., Gastroenterology, 2021, 'conserved metaplasia program in pancreatic injury'; Schlesinger/Alonso-Curbelo, Nat Commun, 2020). HES1 reflects Notch pathway reactivation shown to reprogram acinar cells toward a ductal/progenitor-like state together with oncogenic Kras (De La O et al., PNAS, 2008). CD44 is a recurrent marker of the metaplastic/progenitor-like acinar-derived population in these studies.

states.name: Atrophic/senescent acinar cell
states.phenotype: Reduced enzyme output seen in chronic pancreatitis and aging
states.notes: Direct single-cell transcriptomic characterization of atrophic/senescent human acinar cells is limited, so this panel (9 genes, below the 10-15 target) is built from the general p16/p21/p53 senescence program and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which has been specifically linked to acinar injury: CDKN1A/p21 has been shown to limit senescence and ADM formation during pancreatitis (p21WAF1/Cip1 studies of pancreatitis-associated senescence), and elevated CDKN1A/MDM2/IL6 have been documented in senescent pancreatic stellate/acinar compartments in chronic pancreatitis models. CDKN2A/TP53 are the canonical senescence tumor-suppressor axis; SERPINE1/IL6/IL1B/CXCL1/MMP3 are core SASP factors. Flagging this state as genuinely under-supported in the literature relative to the other three acinar states.

programs.name: Fluid and bicarbonate secretion
programs.function: CFTR-driven ductal fluid and bicarbonate secretion

programs.name: Facultative progenitor potential
programs.function: Latent capacity for endocrine/acinar trans-differentiation implicated in regeneration

programs.name: Neoplastic transformation (PanIN/PDAC)
programs.function: KRAS/TP53/CDKN2A/SMAD4-driven progression through pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia to adenocarcinoma

states.name: Mature functional ductal cell
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy ductal cell secreting bicarbonate-rich fluid
states.notes: Canonical ductal identity/transcription factor and fluid-bicarbonate secretion program of the healthy exocrine duct. Standard, well-established ductal cell markers (pancreas single-cell atlases, e.g., Muraro et al., Cell Syst 2016; Baron et al., Cell Syst 2016).

states.name: CFTR-dysfunctional ductal cell
states.phenotype: Impaired bicarbonate/fluid secretion characteristic of cystic fibrosis-related exocrine pancreatic disease
states.notes: Loss/dysfunction of CFTR is the direct cause of impaired ductal bicarbonate-fluid secretion in CF-related exocrine pancreatic disease (Wine/Reddy, J Cell Sci, 1993 on CFTR and MUC1 co-expression in human ductal cells; 'CFTR, Mucins and Mucus Obstruction in Cystic Fibrosis', Cold Spring Harb Perspect Med, 2012). MUC1/MUC6/TFF2 reflect mucus hypersecretion and inspissation characteristic of the CF duct. SPINK1 is a well-documented genetic modifier of pancreatic disease severity that interacts with CFTR genotype. PDX1 up-regulation has recently been reported as a consequence of CFTR loss altering ductal cell fate ('CFTR represses a PDX1 axis to govern pancreatic ductal cell fate', 2024). This panel is intentionally at 10 genes because ductal-cell-intrinsic transcriptomic data specific to CF (as opposed to CF lung epithelium) is comparatively sparse.

states.name: PanIN-like transformed ductal cell
states.phenotype: Early neoplastic ductal lesion driven by oncogenic KRAS, a precursor to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
states.notes: KRAS/TP53/CDKN2A/SMAD4 are the canonical, sequentially acquired driver alterations of the PanIN-to-PDAC progression model (Hruban et al. PanIN grading/progression scheme). MUC5AC/MUC4/MUC1/MUC6 mucin re-expression is a hallmark of PanIN lesions, with MUC4 reported to appear very early and to associate with activated stromal fibroblasts (Andrianifahanana et al.; 'Oncogenic KRAS, MUC4, and Activin A-mediated fibroblast activation cooperate for PanIN initiation', 2023). S100P expression increases progressively with PanIN grade and is enriched relative to comparable biliary lesions. CEACAM5 is absent in normal ducts and increases with increasing PanIN grade. TFF1/TFF2/CLDN18/KRT17 are recurrent markers of the pyloric/gastric-like metaplastic epithelium seen in PanIN lesions.

states.name: Inflamed ductal cell
states.phenotype: Cytokine exposure typical of chronic pancreatitis
states.notes: Single-cell RNA-seq of mouse pancreas in chronic pancreatitis found several hundred differentially expressed genes specifically in the ductal compartment, broadly reflecting NF-kB-pathway inflammatory activation ('Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis of the Mouse Pancreas: Characteristic Features of Pancreatic Ductal Cells in Chronic Pancreatitis', Genes, 2022). CXCL8 signaling through CXCR2 is required for neutrophil recruitment in pancreatitis, and ductal-derived CCL20-CCR6 chemokine crosstalk with Th17 cells has been specifically identified by single-cell profiling of human chronic pancreatitis. ICAM1/PTGS2(COX2)/SAA1 reflect the acute-phase/adhesion-molecule response of inflamed epithelium seen broadly in chronic pancreatitis. This panel (10 genes) involves more extrapolation from general epithelial inflammatory biology than the other ductal states, since ductal-cell-specific (as opposed to whole-tissue or immune-cell) cytokine profiling in human chronic pancreatitis remains limited.

programs.name: Vitamin A / retinoid storage
programs.function: Cytoplasmic lipid droplets storing retinyl esters, hallmark of the quiescent state

programs.name: Myofibroblast activation
programs.function: Trans-differentiation into a proliferative, contractile myofibroblast-like phenotype

programs.name: Extracellular matrix production
programs.function: Collagen and fibronectin deposition driving fibrosis

programs.name: Apoptosis
programs.function: Programmed cell death; a mechanism of fibrosis resolution

states.name: Quiescent stellate cell
states.phenotype: Vitamin A-storing, non-proliferative resting state in the healthy pancreas
states.notes: GFAP/DES/NES/VIM are classic quiescent pancreatic stellate cell (PSC) cytoskeletal markers shared with hepatic stellate cell biology; RBP1/LRAT/ADH1B reflect the retinoid (vitamin A) storage and metabolism program that defines the quiescent phenotype; PPARG maintains the quiescent state and is lost upon activation (Apte et al.; McCarroll/Bachem PSC reviews).

states.name: Activated myofibroblast-like stellate cell
states.phenotype: Fibrogenic activation driven by injury/inflammation in pancreatitis and PDAC stroma
states.notes: Myofibroblast transdifferentiation markers (ACTA2/TAGLN/S100A4) plus the TGF-beta/SMAD3-driven fibrogenic ECM-production program (COL1A1/COL1A2/COL3A1/FN1/CTGF) and matrix remodeling (MMP2/TIMP1) that define activated PSCs in pancreatitis and PDAC desmoplasia (Apte et al.; Omary et al., J Clin Invest, 2007, PSC biology review).

states.name: Fibrotic (end-stage) stellate cell
states.phenotype: Sustained ECM deposition characteristic of chronic-pancreatitis fibrosis
states.notes: Distinguishes end-stage fibrotic stellate cells from actively-activating cells by emphasizing collagen cross-linking (LOX/LOXL2) and ECM maturation/proteoglycan genes (SPARC, POSTN/periostin, DCN, BGN) alongside sustained high TIMP1 (favoring net ECM accumulation over degradation). POSTN is a well-documented marker of desmoplastic fibrotic stroma in chronic pancreatitis and PDAC (Erkan et al. desmoplasia studies).

states.name: Reverting (quiescing) stellate cell
states.phenotype: Partial return toward quiescence during fibrosis resolution
states.notes: This panel (7 genes, below the 10-15 target) is explicitly extrapolated from hepatic stellate cell (HSC) fibrosis-regression biology rather than direct in vivo pancreatic evidence: Kisseleva et al. (PNAS, 2012) showed that myofibroblasts reverting to an inactive phenotype during regression of liver fibrosis down-regulate ACTA2/COL1A1/TIMP1 while up-regulating the quiescence genes PPARG and BAMBI. Pancreatic stellate cell literature confirms in vitro deactivation upon matrigel/N-acetylcysteine exposure with re-accumulation of retinoid-storage markers (RBP1/LRAT/ADH1B) and cytoskeletal quiescence markers (GFAP/DES), but review literature explicitly states it remains unclear whether PSCs revert to quiescence in vivo, so this state is flagged as having the thinnest direct evidence base of the four stellate states.

programs.name: Leukocyte adhesion
programs.function: Adhesion molecule upregulation enabling immune-cell trafficking into tissue

states.name: Quiescent endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Resting vascular endothelium maintaining normal islet/exocrine perfusion and barrier integrity
states.notes: Core endothelial identity/junctional/barrier genes plus the nitric-oxide (NOS3/GUCY1A1) and anti-thrombotic (THBD) programs of resting endothelium. KLF2/KLF4 are the classic laminar-shear-stress-induced transcription factors that actively enforce and mark the quiescent, anti-inflammatory endothelial phenotype (SenBanerjee et al.; Dekker et al., Blood, 2002/2006).

states.name: Angiogenic endothelial cell
states.phenotype: VEGF-driven vascular remodeling seen in islet growth, wound healing, and tumor neovascularization
states.notes: VEGFA/KDR/FLT1/PGF are the core VEGF-receptor angiogenic axis. DLL4 is the canonical marker of angiogenic 'tip cells' that lead sprouting vessels via Notch signaling (Hellstrom et al., Nature, 2007). ESM1 (endocan) is a well-established marker of tip-cell-like activated angiogenic endothelium (Rocha et al.). APLN/APLNR and PDGFB mark proliferating/sprouting tip and stalk cells; ANGPT2 destabilizes vessels to permit VEGF-driven remodeling, consistent with islet vascular growth, wound healing, and tumor neovascularization.

states.name: Inflamed/activated endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Cytokine-activated endothelium recruiting leukocytes, characteristic of insulitis and pancreatitis
states.notes: ICAM1/VCAM1/SELE/SELP are the canonical NF-kB-induced leukocyte adhesion molecules of activated endothelium. CXCL8/CCL2/CX3CL1 are endothelial-derived chemokines recruiting neutrophils/monocytes. CXCL10 is specifically well documented as a major chemokine produced by activated islet microvasculature/epithelium during insulitis, recruiting CXCR3+ T cells in type 1 diabetes pathogenesis (Uno et al.; Christen et al. insulitis literature). NFKBIA/TNFAIP3 mark the NF-kB activation/negative-feedback signature underlying this state.

states.name: Senescent/dysfunctional endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Reduced barrier integrity and nitric-oxide signaling associated with vascular aging and diabetes-related microangiopathy
states.notes: CDKN2A(p16)/CDKN1A(p21)/TP53 are the core senescence cell-cycle-arrest program, shown to be up-regulated in diabetic/high-glucose-exposed endothelial cells (retinal and wound endothelium senescence studies). SERPINE1/PAI-1 is both a marker and functional mediator of endothelial senescence, elevated in diabetic retinopathy vitreous fluid (Vasile et al.; 'PAI-1 Is a Marker and a Mediator of Senescence', ATVB). THBS1 (thrombospondin-1) mediates diabetes-induced endothelial senescence via CD47 signaling and impaired angiogenesis. IL6/IL1B/CXCL8/MMP3 are core SASP factors. NOS3 and CLDN5 are included as down-regulated markers reflecting the reduced nitric-oxide signaling and barrier integrity that define this dysfunctional state, consistent with diabetes-related microangiopathy.

states.name: Naive/quiescent T cell
states.phenotype: Circulating, antigen-inexperienced T cell
states.notes: Classic circulating naive/quiescent T cell signature: lymph-node homing receptors (CCR7, SELL/CD62L, S1PR1), survival/quiescence factors (IL7R, BCL2 pathway via KLF2), and stemness/naive transcription factors (TCF7, LEF1, BACH2, SATB1) that are downregulated upon effector or exhaustion differentiation. CD27/CD28 costimulatory receptors are progressively lost with differentiation, marking naive/early memory status.

states.name: Cytotoxic activated T cell
states.phenotype: Autoreactive CD8+ effector state driving beta-cell killing in insulitis, characteristic of type 1 diabetes
states.notes: Effector CD8+ cytotoxic program: cytolytic granule contents (GZMB, GZMA, GZMK, PRF1, NKG7), effector cytokines (IFNG, TNF), the master effector transcription factor TBX21 (T-bet), and canonical early/short-term activation markers CD69 and IL2RA (CD25). KLRG1 marks terminally differentiated short-lived effector cells, consistent with autoreactive effector CD8+ T cells in insulitis.

states.name: Exhausted T cell
states.phenotype: Dysfunctional state arising from chronic antigen exposure, seen in longstanding autoimmune infiltrates and tumors
states.notes: Core chronic-antigen exhaustion signature from Wherry/Kurachi and TOX-driven exhaustion program studies: co-inhibitory receptors PDCD1 (PD-1), LAG3, HAVCR2 (TIM-3), TIGIT, CTLA4, TNFRSF9 (4-1BB); the exhaustion-defining transcription factor TOX with EOMES and BATF; and terminal-exhaustion/dysfunction markers ENTPD1 (CD39) and CD38. CXCL13 marks a well-described exhausted/dysfunctional CD8 subset in tumors and chronic infection.

states.name: Regulatory T cell
states.phenotype: Tolerogenic Treg state restraining autoimmune attack on islets
states.notes: FOXP3 lineage-defining transcription factor plus core Treg suppressive machinery: IL2RA (CD25), CTLA4, TNFRSF18 (GITR), the adenosine-generating ectoenzyme pair ENTPD1 (CD39)/NT5E (CD73), LRRC32 (GARP, latent TGF-beta presentation), and suppressive cytokines IL10/TGFB1. IKZF2 (Helios) and IKZF4 (Eos) are Treg-stabilizing transcription factors; CCR4 marks tissue-homing Tregs.

programs.name: Antibody (immunoglobulin) secretion
programs.function: Plasma-cell differentiation and immunoglobulin production, including islet-autoantibody production in type 1 diabetes

states.name: Naive B cell
states.phenotype: Circulating antigen-inexperienced B cell
states.notes: Core B-cell identity/BCR complex (CD19, MS4A1/CD20, CD79A, CD79B, PAX5) combined with markers that specifically distinguish naive from antigen-experienced B cells: surface IgD (IGHD), TCL1A and FCER2 (CD23), high BACH2, and lymphoid-homing receptors SELL/CCR7 that are lost upon activation/memory formation.

states.name: Activated B cell
states.phenotype: Antigen-engaged, proliferating B cell
states.notes: Antigen/BCR-engagement activation markers (CD69, CD86, CD83, CD40), proliferation program (MYC, MKI67, CCND2), and germinal-center/plasmablast-commitment transcription factors (IRF4, BATF, NFKB1). AICDA (AID) marks activated germinal-center B cells undergoing somatic hypermutation/class switching; GPR183 (EBI2) directs activated B cell positioning.

states.name: Antibody-secreting (plasma-like) B cell
states.phenotype: Terminally differentiated antibody-secreting state implicated in islet-autoantibody production in type 1 diabetes
states.notes: Canonical terminal plasma-cell differentiation program (Nutt et al., Nat Rev Immunol 2015): master regulators PRDM1 (BLIMP1), XBP1, IRF4, POU2AF1 (OCA-B); secretory-pathway/ER genes JCHAIN and MZB1; surface plasma cell markers SDC1 (CD138), TNFRSF17 (BCMA), SLAMF7, CD27; and secreted immunoglobulin transcripts IGHG1/IGHM consistent with autoantibody-producing plasma cells in T1D.

states.name: Memory B cell
states.phenotype: Long-lived antigen-experienced B cell poised for rapid recall response
states.notes: CD27 remains the most widely used human memory B cell marker despite known caveats (not universal, can be modulated by IL-21), so it is paired with a broader consensus memory panel: CD80/CD86 (costimulatory upregulation vs naive), FAS/CD95, TNFRSF13B (TACI), CR2 (CD21), CD24, CXCR4 (tissue recall homing), and class-switched IGHG1 transcript. Kept to 10 genes given genuine heterogeneity/lack of a single definitive memory B marker in the literature.

programs.name: M2 reparative/alternative polarization
programs.function: Alternatively activated, tissue-remodeling and anti-inflammatory program

states.name: Resident homeostatic macrophage
states.phenotype: Tissue-resident macrophage maintaining homeostasis and efferocytosis in the healthy pancreas
states.notes: Homeostatic tissue-resident macrophage identity conserved across organs: self-renewal/identity receptor CSF1R, complement/efferocytosis genes (C1QA, C1QB, MERTK, GAS6, VSIG4) supporting apoptotic-cell clearance, and resident-macrophage-specific surface markers LYVE1, TIMD4, FOLR2 that distinguish long-lived resident populations from recruited monocyte-derived macrophages.

states.name: M1 inflammatory macrophage
states.phenotype: Classically activated macrophage driving insulitis and acute-pancreatitis inflammation
states.notes: Classical LPS/IFN-gamma-driven M1 polarization signature (Murray et al., Immunity 2014; Jablonski et al. 2015 gene-signature study): iNOS (NOS2), pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL1B, IL6, IL12B), Th1-recruiting chemokines CXCL9/CXCL10/CXCL11, costimulatory CD86, and the M1-driving transcription factor IRF5. CCR7 and PTGS2 (COX2) are additional established M1 markers.

states.name: M2 reparative macrophage
states.phenotype: Alternatively activated macrophage supporting tissue repair and fibrosis, also resembling tumor-associated macrophages in PDAC
states.notes: Alternatively-activated/wound-healing macrophage program: canonical M2 receptors MRC1 (CD206), CD163, CD36, STAB1, MSR1, CLEC10A; arginase metabolic switch ARG1; anti-inflammatory/pro-fibrotic cytokines IL10 and TGFB1; and tissue-repair factors PDGFB and FN1 (fibronectin) reflecting the reparative/fibrogenic role described in pancreatic tissue repair and PDAC stroma.

states.name: Tumor-associated macrophage
states.phenotype: Immunosuppressive macrophage phenotype supporting tumor growth in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
states.notes: PDAC-specific TAM signature drawn from recent single-cell TAM atlases: SPP1+/TREM2+/APOE+/C1QC+ TAM subsets are recurrently identified pro-tumorigenic populations in PDAC scRNA-seq (e.g. CTHRC1+ fibroblast/SPP1+ macrophage crosstalk papers; MARCO+ TAM characterization in PDAC, PMID 41577813). Immunosuppressive checkpoint/enzyme genes CD274 (PD-L1) and IDO1, plus angiogenic VEGFA and matrix-remodeling MMP9, reflect the immunosuppressive, pro-angiogenic TAM phenotype supporting tumor growth.

programs.name: Degranulation
programs.function: Release of preformed histamine and protease-containing granules

programs.name: Fibrogenic crosstalk
programs.function: Protease and cytokine signaling implicated in promoting pancreatic-stellate-cell activation and fibrosis

states.name: Resting mast cell
states.phenotype: Quiescent tissue-resident mast cell
states.notes: Baseline tissue-resident mast cell identity/differentiation program: KIT (CD117, mast cell growth-factor receptor), the full complement of stored granule proteases (TPSAB1, TPSB2, CMA1, CPA3) present but not yet released, FCER1A/MS4A2 (IgE receptor complex) constitutively expressed, and lineage transcription factors GATA2/MITF. HPGDS, SLC18A2, and IL1RL1 (ST2) reflect steady-state mast cell identity rather than an activation state.

states.name: Degranulated/activated mast cell
states.phenotype: IgE-triggered or injury-triggered degranulation releasing histamine and proteases, implicated in acute pancreatitis and allergic-type responses
states.notes: IgE/FcepsilonRI-triggered degranulation and downstream cytokine program: proximal signaling (FCER1A, MS4A2, SYK), histamine synthesis (HDC), released granule proteases (TPSAB1, CMA1), and newly synthesized cytokines/chemokines (IL6, TNF, CXCL8, IL13) characteristic of acute activation. CD63 and ENPP3 (CD203c) are established surface activation/degranulation markers used by flow cytometry to identify degranulated mast cells/basophils.

states.name: Fibrogenic mast cell
states.phenotype: Chronic activation state implicated in promoting pancreatic fibrosis via stellate-cell crosstalk
states.notes: Evidence for a distinct transcriptionally-defined 'fibrogenic' mast cell state is limited; this panel is built from literature on mast cell-fibroblast/stellate-cell crosstalk (mast cell tryptase/chymase activating fibroblasts and stellate cells; mast cell-derived TGF-beta1 driving PSC activation and fibrosis, e.g. PMC6468868 in PDAC) plus general pro-fibrotic/angiogenic mast cell mediators (VEGFA, FGF2, IL13, TIMP1). Kept to 8 genes (below the 10-15 target) because direct single-cell evidence for this specific state is thin rather than padding with generic mast cell identity genes.

states.name: Degranulation-exhausted mast cell
states.phenotype: Post-degranulation refractory state with depleted granule stores
states.notes: No published transcriptomic signature specifically labeled 'exhausted/post-degranulation refractory mast cell' was found; this is the least literature-supported state in the panel. Genes are inferred from mast cell desensitization/hyporesponsiveness biology (a 2026 bioRxiv study on IgE-mediated mast cell desensitization describes an immunoregulatory transcriptional program distinct from activation, though its specific gene list was not accessible) and general negative-feedback regulators of FcepsilonRI signaling: inhibitory receptors CD200R1 and CD300A, negative signaling regulators SOCS1/SOCS3, the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL10, and retained IgE-receptor complex genes FCER1A/MS4A2 (receptor internalization/downregulation being a hallmark of the refractory state). Given the thinness of direct evidence, only 7 genes are provided rather than padding to 10-15.

references.citation: Talchai C, Xuan S, Lin HV, Sussel L, Accili D. Pancreatic β cell dedifferentiation as a mechanism of diabetic β cell failure. Cell. 2012;150(6):1223-1234. PMID: 22980982
references.note: Foundational beta-cell dedifferentiation model: loss of identity genes, gain of progenitor markers (Neurog3, Sox9, Aldh1a3), FOXO1 nuclear exclusion, and emergence of alpha-cell-like markers underlying the dedifferentiated and transdifferentiated beta-cell states.

references.citation: Cinti F, Bouchi R, Kim-Muller JY, et al. Evidence of β-Cell Dedifferentiation in Human Type 2 Diabetes. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(3):1044-1054. PMID: 26713822

references.citation: Pullen TJ, Rutter GA. When less is more: the forbidden fruits of gene repression in the adult β-cell. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2013;15(6):503-512.
references.note: Defines 'disallowed genes' (LDHA, SLC16A1/MCT1) whose re-expression marks loss of beta-cell identity, used in the dedifferentiated state.

references.citation: Spijker HS, Song H, Ellenbroek JH, et al. Loss of β-Cell Identity Occurs in Type 2 Diabetes and Is Associated With Islet Amyloid Deposits. Diabetes. 2015;64(8):2928-2938.
references.note: Human evidence for beta-to-alpha cell transdifferentiation (co-expression of ARX/MAFB/GCG in insulin-lineage cells), supporting the transdifferentiated beta-cell state.

references.citation: Human pancreatic α-cell heterogeneity and trajectory inference analyses reveal SMOC1 as a β-cell dedifferentiation gene. Nat Commun. 2025. PMID: 41057332
references.note: Identifies SMOC1 as an alpha-lineage gene ectopically induced along the beta-to-alpha dedifferentiation/transdifferentiation trajectory in human T2D islets.

references.citation: Aguayo-Mazzucato C, Andle J, Lee TB Jr, et al. Acceleration of β Cell Aging Determines Diabetes and Senolysis Improves Disease Outcomes. Cell Metab. 2019;30(1):129-142. PMID: 31155496

references.citation: Thompson PJ, Shah A, Ntranos V, et al. Targeted Elimination of Senescent Beta Cells Prevents Type 1 Diabetes. Cell Metab. 2019;29(5):1045-1060.
references.note: Characterizes the beta-cell senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP: GDF15, SERPINE1, CCL2, IL1B).

references.citation: Zhong L, et al. / FoxM1-related studies (e.g., FoxM1 Is Up-Regulated by Obesity and Stimulates β-Cell Proliferation, Mol Endocrinol 2010; Insulin signaling regulates the FoxM1/PLK1/CENP-A pathway, PMC5382039).
references.note: FOXM1/CCND2/PLK1/CENPA/BIRC5 as drivers of adaptive human beta-cell proliferation in obesity and pregnancy, supporting the proliferating beta-cell state.

references.citation: Xin Y, Gutierrez GD, Okamoto H, et al. and related human islet single-cell studies characterizing alpha-cell-enriched genes LOXL4, CRYBA2, GC, and SLC7A2.

references.citation: Adriaenssens AE, Svendsen B, Lam BY, et al. Transcriptomic profiling of pancreatic alpha, beta and delta cell populations identifies delta cells as a principal target for ghrelin in mouse islets. Diabetologia. 2016;59(10):2156-2165.

references.citation: Somatostatin Containing δ-Cell Number Is Reduced in Type-2 Diabetes. PMC9959292.

references.citation: Dean ED, Li M, Prasad N, et al. Interrupted Glucagon Signaling Reveals Hepatic α Cell Axis and Role for L-Glutamine in α Cell Proliferation. Cell Metab. 2017; and Pancreatic islet α cell function and proliferation require the arginine transporter SLC7A2. JCI 2024.
